directions.name: A — Loose cut shapes
directions.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one landscape illustration art-direction specimen board for Hey Kahani, a playful and thoughtful children's storytelling brand. This is an exploratory illustration system for a WEBSITE ONLY, NOT a logo, storybook cover or a finished website. White background. No typography, words, letters, numbers, labels, swatches, watermarks, human figures or product hardware.
CONSISTENT CONTENT AND LAYOUT: top two-thirds of the board is six generously spaced standalone illustrations arranged loosely in three columns and two rows. Top row: a flying paper kite with curling string, a small fresh mango-leaf sprig, a marigold flower with simple stem. Second row: an open storybook releasing a small curved sound trail, an irregular sunshine motif, an expressive abstract squiggle plus pebble-shape cluster. All objects must be fully visible, strong simple silhouettes, few purposeful details. Bottom third: a wide Kesar Sand cream band with softly irregular top boundary, left half intentionally blank as website headline space, right half a compact playful composition combining the same book, sprig and kite visual language, showing how these illustrations support website content. Generous blank margins and thoughtful calm space; cheerful and visibly for kids.
PALETTE: use flat colours from Hey Kahani only: Gulab Red #D3000A, Kesar Sand #FFF1D6, Sky Blue #63C3FE, Mango Yellow #FECB74, Story Ink #05334A, Parrot Green #2B9863; very occasional Marigold Orange #FF5D27 or Lavender tea #D6C9E4 accent. Primary red/sand/sky/yellow establish the identity; green supports plants. Keep the same palette across the whole board; never a rainbow confetti collage. Plant/object references give a subtle South Asian everyday character without cliché or ornate decorative festival imagery.
EXPRESSION: predominantly FACELESS. Do not add faces to plants, flowers, kite or book. At most one tiny two-stroke sleepy expression on the sunshine, subordinate and optional; personality primarily from posture, contour and placement.
DRAWING: free imperfect hand-drawn shapes, raw in a deliberate charming way, never pixel-perfect stock icons. No gradients, lighting, glossy 3D, shadows, photorealism or detailed scenery. Aim for shapes that can later be redrawn as editable SVG. Maintain genuine difference of drawing grammar specified below.
STYLE A: Bold irregular filled silhouettes as if intuitively cut freehand with scissors, but entirely flat vector-like digital colours and no physical paper material. Soft asymmetry, broad rounded shapes, slightly wonky organic contours, confident simple masses, rounded uneven sun rays. Use only a few thin dark ink details, such as a leaf central vein or book fold. Most shapes have NO outline. Kite panels are uneven curved quadrants, flower petals are irregular rounded lobes, book pages are soft chunky shapes. Friendly, immediate, restrained. No grain texture, no crosshatching, no decorative patterns. The charm comes from silhouette alone. Colour carries nearly all of the illustration.

STYLE B: Line-led freehand doodle language. Visible loosely wandering Story Ink strokes have small natural changes of thickness, occasional gaps, relaxed loops and tiny overshoots. Mostly open white interiors; selective rough flat colour patches sit slightly off the line, not fully colouring everything. At least 65 percent of the object interior area remains white. Kite traced by an imperfect ink loop with just one blue patch; loose book outlined in wandering ink with a single red cover patch; botanical sprig gestural and playful with green selective fills; marigold from looping scribble line and yellow central dab; sun an incomplete circular ink loop and loose rays. Very sparse deliberate hatching, no solid chunky cut-paper style. Airy, lively, human-drawn rather than cartoon stock illustration. Raw expressive gesture but readable at small website scale.

STYLE C: Chunky irregular hand-carved rubber stamp and simple block-print illustration, translated into vector-friendly shapes. Bold solid simplified silhouettes with slightly jagged or wavy edges and a few thick carved-out negative-space notches and grooves. Very light sparse ink skips confined to edges; NO all-over paper grain, stippling or photographic print simulation. Colours remain saturated and flat. Sun is an uneven round stamped disc with thick blunt tapered rays, marigold has broad asymmetrical petals with cream notches, leaves use bold green masses with chunky cream vein cuts. Book pages indicated by a few broad unprinted cream slits rather than fine lines. Kite feels a wonky printed lozenge with large two-colour blocks. Strong tactile handmade identity, playful and thoughtful, contemporary with subtle Indian printmaking warmth, never ornate folk-art borders. No external dark outlines.

STYLE D: Playful assembled shapes with loose drawn patterns. Construct every object from 3-6 oversized irregular component shapes: off-round circles, soft wedges, bent strips, uneven arches. Visible overlaps between opaque contrasting flat components, deliberately off-centre joins and slightly surprising proportions. Mix big plain colour masses with one simple hand-drawn pattern per object maximum: 3 wonky stripes, 4 loose dots or an uneven grid. A kite assembled from four misaligned curved colour panels; plant leaves from imperfect tilted ovals on a bent strip stem; marigold assembled from uneven petal shapes with a single patterned centre; book assembled from 4 irregular curved page panels with one scribbled line; sun assembled from irregular disc and alternating blunt wedges. No precision symmetry or strict geometry, no perfect circles or polished icon look. Colourful curious construction-toy energy, but thoughtful whitespace and simple readable silhouettes. No print texture and no full outlines. Clearly distinguish this modular patterned language from continuous silhouettes and from line doodles.
